CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with history of recurrent kidney stones; also here for management of hypertension and diabetes.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports pain related to kidney stone that has been "up and down." She went to the emergency room last week and believes the stone passed approximately three days ago. She denies current blood in urine and denies current pain. This is her seventh or eighth kidney stone. She received pain medication (Percocet) at the hospital. Last visit was with a urologist approximately one year ago.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies chest pain and abdominal pain. Patient reports occasional insomnia with worry and has tried meditation apps which help. She uses sleep mode inconsistently and keeps phone by bed and TV on during sleep. Tried melatonin a couple times with minimal benefit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus type 2 (diagnosed one year ago)
Recurrent kidney stones (7-8 episodes)
Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur (known, unchanged)
Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty avoiding fast food due to being "on the go" and limited time for food preparation. Home blood pressure readings typically 130-140 over 60-70.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure at visit: 150/90 (noted as slightly high). Lungs clear bilaterally, no crackles. Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted, unchanged from prior. Abdomen: No tenderness to palpation. Costovertebral angle: No tenderness on right side.

RESULTS
Last A1C: 6.7 (slightly elevated, improved from initial diagnosis)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stones: Likely passed. Will obtain urinalysis and urine culture. Referral to urology with Dr. Harris for recurrent kidney stone evaluation and management.
Hypertension: Currently controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. Continue current dose. Likely has white coat syndrome. Continue home blood pressure monitoring 2-3 times weekly. Continue current refills.
Diabetes mellitus type 2: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient instructed to check blood sugars before each meal to better gauge dietary intake.
Hypertension and diabetes management: Referral to nutrition consultation to address dietary modifications, target sodium intake <2300 mg daily.
Insomnia: Start melatonin 10 mg as needed. Encouraged to practice proper sleep hygiene including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and using sleep mode on phone.
Follow-up: Return visit in 3 months.
